title: CS-06 Customer Satisfaction: declared formula, numerator and denominator with honest missing-data behaviour
risk: The Customer Satisfaction figure is produced under different accounting rules - the mean published with no response rate, so ten responses are presented as the voice of twenty customers - so the KPI is wrong in the direction that flatters the programme and every decision taken on it inherits the error.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
Metric scope is fixed before measurement: numerator is survey scores from customer responses; denominator is surveys sent, published as the response rate.
The dictionary entry for 'Customer Satisfaction' (owner, unit, window, exclusion rule) is loaded read-only and is compared with the recomputation instead of being trusted.

inputs.formula: mean survey score with the response rate published alongside it
inputs.expected_value: 4.7 out of 5 with a response rate of 50.0%
inputs.wrong_value_if_buggy: the mean published with no response rate, so ten responses are presented as the voice of twenty customers
inputs.expected_boundary_behaviour: no survey response in the window reports NO_DATA, never a score of 0 and never a default of 5

steps.action: Compute Customer Satisfaction from the frozen rows in kpi_dataset.care
steps.expected: The stored aggregate reports 4.7 out of 5 with a response rate of 50.0% and records the formula, the window and the currency that produced it.

steps.action: Recompute Customer Satisfaction independently from the raw counter rows for the same tenant and window
steps.expected: The recomputed value equals the stored value 4.7 out of 5 with a response rate of 50.0%, and every numerator row lies inside the denominator scope.

steps.action: Force the empty-source variant of the metric (no qualifying row in the window)
steps.expected: The metric reports no survey response in the window reports NO_DATA, never a score of 0 and never a default of 5; the display distinguishes missing source data from a measured zero.

steps.action: Read the dashboard payload and the metric dictionary entry
steps.expected: The dashboard renders the stored value with its window, coverage and source, and the dictionary names the owner, unit, numerator and denominator that the recomputation used.

assertions: Customer Satisfaction equals 4.7 out of 5 with a response rate of 50.0% for the frozen window, recomputed from the raw counter rows with numerator scope 'survey scores from customer responses' and denominator scope 'surveys sent, published as the response rate'.

A recomputation that yields the mean published with no response rate, so ten responses are presented as the voice of twenty customers is detected as wrong: the stored aggregate and the independent recomputation must agree before the figure is published.
The dashboard payload for the same tenant and window carries the stored value with its window, coverage and measurement source; it substitutes neither a design target nor another metric's value.
Boundary behaviour: no survey response in the window reports NO_DATA, never a score of 0 and never a default of 5; missing source data is never rendered as a measured zero.
forbidden: Publishing the average score without the response rate.
Substituting a default score for the customers who did not respond.
evidence: Survey response extract with the scores.
Survey send count used for the response rate.
cleanup: Delete gov- aggregate, raw-counter and scenario rows for CS-06 after exporting the recomputation table.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
